concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Firewalls › three main firewall architectures

concepts.def: A router filters (screens) traffic before it is passed to the firewall.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Firewalls › three main firewall architectures

concepts.def: is a framing protocol that is used mainly for device-to-device communication
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · WAN Technologies

concepts.def: Provides data integrity, data-origin authentication, and protection from replay attacks
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · VPN › Internet Protocol Security

concepts.def: Provides confidentiality, data-origin authentication, and data integrity
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · VPN › Internet Protocol Security

concepts.def: Provides authenticated keying material for use with ISAKMP
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · VPN › Internet Protocol Security

concepts.def: it provides a framework to enable many types of authentication techniques to be used when establishing network connections.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Authentication Protocols

concepts.def: is a standard for encrypting and digitally signing e-mail and for providing secure data transmissions.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · E-mail Encryption Standards

concepts.def: A drive-by download occurs when a user visits a website that is hosting malicious code and automatically gets infected.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Network Attacks
ID = who you claim to be. Auth = prove it.
concepts.def: Identification claims an identity; authentication proves it with evidence.
concepts.ex: Username = identification; password/token = authentication.

concepts.tip: Strong auth = MFA. Two of: know, have, are, location, behavior.
concepts.def: Requires two or more independent authentication factors from different categories (MFA).
concepts.ex: Password + OTP token = something you know + something you have.

concepts.tip: LDAP = directory access protocol. Port 389 (636 for TLS).
concepts.def: Protocol for accessing and maintaining X.500 directory services over TCP/IP (port 389/636).
concepts.ex: Active Directory uses LDAP for querying user and group information.

concepts.tip: X.500 = directory standard. DN hierarchy: CN, OU, O, C.
concepts.def: ITU standard defining hierarchical directory service structure using Distinguished Names (DN).
concepts.ex: DN: CN=John Doe, OU=Sales, O=Company, C=US.

concepts.tip: Directory = single source of truth for identities.
concepts.def: Centralized repositories storing user identities, attributes, credentials, and group memberships.
concepts.ex: Active Directory is the authoritative identity store for most enterprises.

concepts.tip: Auth methods: know it, have it, are it, where you are, how you act.
concepts.def: Knowledge (passwords), possession (tokens), inherence (biometrics), location, and behavior.
concepts.ex: ATM uses card (possession) + PIN (knowledge) — two-factor auth.

concepts.tip: Credential mgmt = centralized secure storage and lifecycle for credentials.
concepts.def: Privileged access managers, password vaults, and SSO handling the full credential lifecycle.
concepts.ex: CyberArk vaults privileged passwords; LastPass manages employee credentials.

concepts.tip: Biometrics: FRR vs FAR. CER = crossover = equal error rate.
concepts.def: Authentication using physiological (fingerprint, iris) or behavioral (typing rhythm) traits.
concepts.ex: FRR (false reject = inconvenience), FAR (false accept = security breach), CER (crossover).

concepts.tip: Passwords = most common auth. Long + complex + unique per site.
concepts.def: Shared secret strings used for authentication — most common but vulnerable to many attacks.
concepts.ex: Weak passwords cracked in seconds; long passphrases resist brute force.

concepts.tip: Password policy: length + complexity + expiry + lockout.
concepts.def: Rules enforcing complexity, minimum length, expiry, history, and lockout to strengthen passwords.
concepts.ex: Policy: 12+ chars, mixed case + numbers + symbols, 90-day expiry, 10 history.

concepts.tip: Password checker = strength meter. Catches common and weak choices.
concepts.def: Tools evaluating password strength against dictionary lists and complexity rules.
concepts.ex: zxcvbn library scores password entropy; enterprise tools enforce policy compliance.

concepts.tip: OTP = use once then discard. HOTP (counter) or TOTP (30-sec timer).
concepts.def: Dynamically generated password valid for a single authentication — HOTP (counter-based) or TOTP (time-based).
concepts.ex: Google Authenticator generates TOTP codes that expire every 30 seconds.

concepts.tip: Crypto keys = the secret that makes encryption work. Protect them!
concepts.def: Secret values used in symmetric or asymmetric encryption algorithms for authentication and data protection.
concepts.ex: AES-256 symmetric key; RSA-4096 key pair for PKI.

concepts.tip: Smart card attacks: SPA, DPA, fault injection, microprobing.
concepts.def: Physical and side-channel attacks against smart card chips including power analysis and fault injection.
concepts.ex: Simple Power Analysis (SPA) reveals crypto operations from power consumption traces.

concepts.tip: Side-channel = physical leakage, not math. Timing, power, EM.
concepts.def: Attacks exploiting physical information (power consumption, timing, EM emissions) to extract cryptographic secrets.
concepts.ex: Timing attack measures decryption time to infer private key bits.

concepts.tip: Authorization = what you're ALLOWED to do after authentication.
concepts.def: Determining what resources and operations an authenticated subject is permitted to access.
concepts.ex: ACL grants user read access to /sales but denies write access.

concepts.tip: Access criteria = the conditions under which access is granted.
concepts.def: Rules determining access decisions: identity, role, time of day, location, classification level.
concepts.ex: Access allowed only during business hours from corporate IP addresses.

concepts.tip: SSO = authenticate once, access everywhere. Kerberos and SAML enable it.
concepts.def: One authentication event grants access to multiple systems without requiring re-authentication.
concepts.ex: Log in to AD once; access email, CRM, and ERP without logging in again.

concepts.tip: Kerberos = tickets. KDC → TGT → service ticket. No passwords on wire.
concepts.def: Ticket-based authentication protocol using a Key Distribution Center (KDC) and symmetric cryptography.
concepts.ex: KDC issues TGT; TGT used to get service tickets for specific resources.

concepts.tip: Kerberos: KDC (AS+TGS) → TGT → service ticket → access.
concepts.def: Key Distribution Center (KDC) with Authentication Server (AS) and Ticket Granting Server (TGS); TGT; service tickets; principals.
concepts.ex: Client gets TGT from AS, then service ticket from TGS, then accesses service.

concepts.def: Secret keys are temporarily stored on the users’ workstations, which means it is possible for an intruder to obtain these cryptographic keys.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Single Sign-On › Kerberos
Security domain = trust bubble. Same policy inside.
concepts.def: Groups of subjects and objects operating under the same security policy and trust level.
concepts.ex: HR domain: only HR users and their systems; separate from Finance domain.

concepts.tip: Directory service = centralized identity and resource phonebook.
concepts.def: Network services providing centralized storage and lookup of resource information and identities.
concepts.ex: Active Directory, OpenLDAP, eDirectory — all directory services.

concepts.tip: Thin client = dumb terminal. Less to attack locally.
concepts.def: Lightweight endpoint devices relying on a server for processing, reducing the local attack surface.
concepts.ex: Terminal in call center: runs only display protocol, no local data stored.

concepts.tip: Accountability = audit trail. Who did what, when. Non-repudiation.
concepts.def: Tracking and logging user actions to specific identities for audit trails and non-repudiation.
concepts.ex: Audit log records: who accessed what, when, from where, and what they did.

concepts.tip: App-level events = what happened inside the application.
concepts.def: Events logged within applications capturing user actions like login, data access, and configuration changes.
concepts.ex: ERP system logs: user X modified order #1234 at 14:32.

concepts.tip: User-level events = individual user audit trail. Login, access, changes.
concepts.def: OS and application logs recording individual user activities for accountability.
concepts.ex: Windows Security Event Log: user logon, logoff, failed login attempts.

concepts.tip: Session mgmt = start, maintain, and kill sessions securely.
concepts.def: Controlling active sessions through timeouts, token management, and secure termination.
concepts.ex: Web app invalidates session token on logout; 15-minute idle timeout.

concepts.tip: Federation = trust bridge between organizations. Your IdP, my service.
concepts.def: Cross-organizational trust relationship allowing users to authenticate with their home organization's credentials.
concepts.ex: University student uses university login to access partner hospital system via SAML federation.

concepts.tip: Access markup: SAML (assertions), XACML (policies), SPML (provisioning).
concepts.def: XML-based standards (XACML, SAML, SPML) for exchanging access control policies and assertions.
concepts.ex: XACML expresses fine-grained authorization policies in XML.

concepts.tip: SPML = automate account provisioning. XML-based user lifecycle.
concepts.def: XML-based standard for automating provisioning and deprovisioning of user accounts and resources.
concepts.ex: HR system sends SPML request to provision new employee account in AD.

concepts.tip: SAML = SSO standard. IdP sends XML assertion to service provider.
concepts.def: XML standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity providers and service providers.
concepts.ex: SAML assertion from corporate IdP lets user access SaaS application.

concepts.tip: OpenID = reuse your existing identity account across sites.
concepts.def: Decentralized authentication protocol allowing users to use one identity across multiple websites.
concepts.ex: 'Log in with Google' on a third-party site uses OpenID.

concepts.tip: OAuth = authorize apps to act for you. Access tokens, not passwords.
concepts.def: Authorization framework allowing limited delegated access to resources without sharing credentials.
concepts.ex: Twitter app requests OAuth token to post on your behalf — no password shared.

concepts.tip: OIDC = OAuth 2.0 + identity layer. ID token = who you are.
concepts.def: Authentication layer built on OAuth 2.0 providing identity tokens (JWT) for user authentication.
concepts.ex: 'Sign in with Google' button uses OIDC to return ID token with user info.

concepts.tip: OIDC flows: Auth Code (secure), Implicit (deprecated), Hybrid.
concepts.def: Authorization Code (server-side), Implicit (deprecated for SPAs), and Hybrid (combination) flows.
concepts.ex: Web app server uses Authorization Code flow for secure token exchange.

concepts.def: An on-premise (or on-premises) IdM system is one in which all needed resources remain under your physical control.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Integrating Identity as a Service
IDaaS integration = sync on-prem + cloud identity. Protocol gaps.
concepts.def: Challenges in federating cloud IDaaS with on-premises directory services — protocol, latency, and sync issues.
concepts.ex: Azure AD Connect syncing on-prem AD with Azure AD — conflict resolution needed.

concepts.tip: DAC = owner decides who gets in. Most common OS model.
concepts.def: Resource owners control access to their objects — flexible but management-intensive and user-dependent.
concepts.ex: File owner sets read/write permissions for other users (chmod, Windows ACLs).

concepts.tip: MAC = system decides, not the owner. Labels + clearances.
concepts.def: System-enforced access based on security labels and clearances — users cannot override policy.
concepts.ex: SELinux enforces MAC; users can't change security labels on files.

concepts.tip: Security labels = classification stamp. MAC compares labels to clearances.
concepts.def: Sensitivity markings assigned to subjects and objects in MAC systems to enforce access policy.
concepts.ex: Document labeled SECRET; user cleared SECRET — MAC allows read access.

concepts.tip: RBAC = roles carry permissions. Users get roles, roles get access.
concepts.def: Permissions are assigned to roles; users acquire permissions by being assigned to roles.
concepts.ex: Bank teller role: view accounts, process deposits. Cannot access loan officer functions.

concepts.tip: Core RBAC = users + roles + permissions + sessions. NIST baseline.
concepts.def: Minimum RBAC components: users, roles, permissions, and sessions — the NIST RBAC baseline.
concepts.ex: NIST RBAC standard defines core as: UA (user-role assign), PA (perm-role assign).

concepts.tip: Hierarchical RBAC = roles inherit. Manager > Employee permissions.
concepts.def: Roles inherit permissions from senior roles in a hierarchy — junior roles get subset of senior permissions.
concepts.ex: Manager role inherits all Employee role permissions plus additional approvals.

concepts.tip: ABAC = policy engine evaluates attributes. Most flexible, most complex.
concepts.def: Fine-grained access control based on attributes of users, resources, and environmental conditions.
concepts.ex: Access allowed if user.department=HR AND resource.classification=internal AND time=businessHours.

concepts.tip: Constrained UI = hide what you can't use. Menu-based access control.
concepts.def: Limit available options based on user role — menus, views, or functions hidden from unauthorized users.
concepts.ex: ATM shows only deposit/withdraw; admin console shows all options.

concepts.tip: Remote AAA: RADIUS (UDP), TACACS+ (TCP, Cisco), Diameter (next-gen).
concepts.def: RADIUS, TACACS+, and Diameter for authenticating and authorizing remote network access.
concepts.ex: VPN concentrator sends RADIUS request to authenticate remote worker.

concepts.term: Terminal Access Controller Access Control System (TACACS)
concepts.tip: TACACS/TACACS+ = Cisco AAA for network devices. TCP port 49.
concepts.def: Cisco proprietary AAA protocol for network device access — TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization, and accounting.
concepts.ex: Network admin logs into router; TACACS+ authenticates and authorizes specific commands.

concepts.tip: Diameter = RADIUS successor. TCP-based, more reliable, 4G/LTE networks.
concepts.def: Next-generation AAA protocol replacing RADIUS — more reliable, TCP/SCTP-based, and more extensible.
concepts.ex: LTE 4G networks use Diameter for AAA between HSS and MME.

concepts.tip: Authentication = proof of identity. Something you know/have/are.
concepts.def: Process of verifying the identity claimed during identification through passwords, tokens, or biometrics.
concepts.ex: Password check, fingerprint scan, or OTP verification — all authentication.

concepts.tip: Accounting = logging what was used. Who, what, when, how much.
concepts.def: Recording resource usage, session details, and user actions for billing, audit, and capacity planning.
concepts.ex: RADIUS accounting logs: session start/stop, bytes transferred, duration.

concepts.tip: Access matrix = spreadsheet of who can do what to what.
concepts.def: Table with subjects as rows, objects as columns, and permitted operations as cell values.
concepts.ex: User A: read file1, write file2. User B: read file1 only.

concepts.tip: Content-dependent = what's IN the data determines access.
concepts.def: Access decisions based on the actual content of the requested data, not just the resource name.
concepts.ex: Database view showing only rows where employee.dept = user.dept.

concepts.cat: Managing the Identity and Access Provisioning Life Cycle
concepts.tip: Provisioning = set up access. New user gets accounts and roles.
concepts.def: Creating user accounts, assigning roles, and granting access rights when a user joins or changes roles.
concepts.ex: New employee joins HR; IT provisions AD account, email, and ERP role.

concepts.cat: Managing the Identity and Access Provisioning Life Cycle
concepts.tip: Access review = periodic 'is this still needed?' check. Recertification.
concepts.def: Periodic certification process verifying that users' current access rights remain appropriate.
concepts.ex: Quarterly review: manager certifies each direct report's system access.

concepts.cat: Managing the Identity and Access Provisioning Life Cycle
concepts.tip: System account review = find and fix over-privileged service accounts.
concepts.def: Reviewing service accounts, shared accounts, and privileged system accounts for excessive or unnecessary access.
concepts.ex: Service account review finds accounts with domain admin privilege — remove it.

concepts.tip: Access layers: physical + logical + administrative = defense in depth.
concepts.def: Defense-in-depth using physical, logical, and administrative controls in multiple overlapping layers.
concepts.ex: Physical: locked server room. Logical: firewall + ACLs. Admin: security policies.

concepts.tip: Unauthorized disclosure = confidentiality breach. Insider or accidental.
concepts.def: Accidental or deliberate exposure of sensitive data to unauthorized individuals.
concepts.ex: Employee emails confidential contract to wrong recipient; insider leaks trade secrets.

concepts.tip: Emanation = EM leakage. TEMPEST shields prevent signal interception.
concepts.def: Protecting against unintentional electromagnetic emissions that leak data (TEMPEST program).
concepts.ex: Faraday cage prevents RF signals from laptop from being captured externally.

concepts.tip: IDS = passive monitor. Detects and alerts but doesn't block.
concepts.def: Systems monitoring network traffic or host activity to detect and alert on malicious behavior.
concepts.ex: Snort IDS alerts on SQL injection patterns in web traffic.

concepts.tip: Signature-based = pattern library. Great at known attacks; misses zero-days.
concepts.def: IDS matching observed traffic against database of known attack signatures.
concepts.ex: Snort rule matches network packet to known Metasploit exploit pattern.

concepts.tip: Pattern matching = compare to known bad. Signature IDS and AV method.
concepts.def: Comparing data streams against known malicious patterns in signature databases.
concepts.ex: AV engine compares file bytes to malware signature hash database.

concepts.tip: Anomaly-based = deviation from normal. Catches zero-days; more false positives.
concepts.def: IDS establishing baseline normal behavior and alerting when deviations exceed a threshold.
concepts.ex: User normally downloads 10MB/day — 10GB download triggers anomaly alert.

concepts.tip: Dictionary attack = tries common words. Defend with salted hashes + lockout.
concepts.def: Systematically trying words from a dictionary or wordlist against password hashes or login forms.
concepts.ex: Tool tries 'password', 'qwerty', 'admin123' against MD5 hash dump.

concepts.tip: Countermeasures: lockout + CAPTCHA + MFA + salted hashes.
concepts.def: Account lockout, CAPTCHAs, MFA, salted hashes, and rate limiting defend against password attacks.
concepts.ex: Lock account after 5 failed attempts; require CAPTCHA after 3 failures.

concepts.tip: Brute force = try everything. Long passwords + lockout defeat it.
concepts.def: Systematically trying every possible password combination until the correct one is found.
concepts.ex: 8-char alphanumeric: ~218 trillion combinations; GPU can try billions/sec.

concepts.tip: Spoofing at logon = fake login to steal password. Trusted path defeats it.
concepts.def: Presenting a fake login screen to capture user credentials — a physical or software attack.
concepts.ex: Malware displays fake Windows login screen capturing entered credentials.

concepts.tip: Phishing = fake email/link. Pharming = DNS redirect. Both steal credentials.
concepts.def: Phishing uses deceptive emails/sites; pharming poisons DNS to redirect users to fake sites.
concepts.ex: Phishing email with fake bank link; pharming redirects real URL to attacker site.

concepts.tip: IS audit = systematic evidence review. Plan → collect → analyze → report.
concepts.def: Systematic, evidence-based review of security controls to verify compliance and effectiveness.
concepts.ex: Auditor reviews firewall rules, patch status, access logs, and policies.

concepts.tip: Internal audit = own team reviews. Fast but less independent.
concepts.def: Security reviews conducted by organization's own staff — useful but may lack independence.
concepts.ex: Internal audit team reviews password policy compliance quarterly.

concepts.tip: External audit = independent third party. More objective credibility.
concepts.def: Independent third-party security review providing unbiased assessment of controls.
concepts.ex: Annual SOC 2 Type II audit by independent CPA firm.

concepts.tip: Third-party audit = audit your vendors. Trust but verify supply chain.
concepts.def: Audits conducted on vendors, partners, or suppliers to verify their security controls.
concepts.ex: Enterprise audits cloud provider's security controls before signing contract.

concepts.tip: Facilitate = prepare evidence, assign liaison, grant access. Be ready.
concepts.def: Providing auditors with necessary access, documentation, key personnel contact, and cooperation.
concepts.ex: Assign audit liaison, prepare evidence packages, grant read-only system access.

concepts.tip: Vuln testing = scan for weaknesses. No exploitation — just report.
concepts.def: Scanning systems and applications for known vulnerabilities without actively exploiting them.
concepts.ex: Nessus scan identifies unpatched CVEs on web servers.

concepts.tip: Pen test = authorized attack simulation. Exploits vulns to show real impact.
concepts.def: Authorized simulated attack exploiting vulnerabilities to assess actual risk and impact.
concepts.ex: Pen tester exploits XSS to demonstrate cookie theft and lateral movement.

concepts.tip: War dialing = scan phone numbers for modems. Old-school recon technique.
concepts.def: Automated scanning of large phone number ranges to identify modems, fax machines, and remote access systems.
concepts.ex: ToneLoc tool dials 1000 numbers to find corporate modem banks.

concepts.tip: Other vulns: misconfig, defaults, logic flaws, missing patches.
concepts.def: Configuration errors, insecure defaults, logic flaws, and missing patches beyond software code bugs.
concepts.ex: Default admin credentials on router; misconfigured S3 bucket with public access.

concepts.tip: Log review = find anomalies in audit trail. SIEM helps automate it.
concepts.def: Analyzing system, application, and security logs to detect anomalies, policy violations, and incidents.
concepts.ex: Review firewall logs for outbound connections to known C2 IP addresses.

concepts.tip: Prevent log tampering: remote syslog + WORM + cryptographic signing.
concepts.def: Using write-once media, remote syslog, and integrity monitoring to protect log files from modification.
concepts.ex: Forward logs to immutable SIEM immediately; use cryptographic log signing.

concepts.tip: RUM = watch real user sessions. Detects anomalies in user behavior.
concepts.def: Capturing and analyzing actual end-user interactions with applications for performance and security.
concepts.ex: RUM tool detects unusual session patterns indicating account takeover.

concepts.tip: Account mgmt audit = find orphan accounts, over-privilege, stale access.
concepts.def: Reviewing user accounts for proper provisioning, least-privilege enforcement, and timely deprovisioning.
concepts.ex: Audit finds 47 terminated employees still have active accounts — revoke immediately.

concepts.tip: Modify accounts = keep access aligned with current job function.
concepts.def: Updating user roles, permissions, or account status as job functions change.
concepts.ex: Employee promoted to manager — update role and add approval permissions.

concepts.tip: Backup verification = test restores. Untested backup is not a backup.
concepts.def: Testing that backups are complete, accurate, uncorrupted, and actually restorable.
concepts.ex: Monthly restore test: recover random file from backup; verify contents match.

concepts.tip: Data types: production, test, archive. Different treatment for each.
concepts.def: Classifying data (production, test, backup, archive) to apply appropriate protection and retention.
concepts.ex: Production data: highest protection; test data: anonymized; archive: long-term retention.

concepts.def: Develop scenarios that capture specific sets of events that are representative of the threats facing the organization.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Backup Verification
DR = restore IT. BCP = keep business running. Related but different.
concepts.def: DR restores IT systems; BCP ensures business operations continue after a disruption.
concepts.ex: DR plan: restore servers in 4 hours. BCP: reroute calls to backup call center.

concepts.term: Testing and Revising the Business Continuity Plan
concepts.tip: BCP test = find gaps before a real disaster does.
concepts.def: Validating BCP effectiveness through tests and updating the plan based on findings and organizational changes.
concepts.ex: Annual tabletop simulation reveals gap in supply chain recovery procedures.

concepts.tip: Checklist test = desk review only. Least disruptive, least realistic.
concepts.def: Simplest BCP test — team reviews the plan document for completeness without any simulation.
concepts.ex: Recovery team reads plan, checks each step exists, identifies missing contacts.

concepts.tip: BCP tests: checklist → tabletop → walkthrough → simulation → full interruption.
concepts.def: Tabletop exercises, structured walkthroughs, functional drills, and full-interruption tests for BCP/DR preparedness.
concepts.ex: Tabletop: scenario discussion; full-interruption: actually failover to DR site.

concepts.term: Security Training and Security Awareness Training
concepts.tip: Training = skills for your role. Awareness = culture for everyone.
concepts.def: Training provides role-specific skills; awareness builds general security culture across all staff.
concepts.ex: Developers get secure coding training; all staff get phishing awareness training.

concepts.tip: KPI = are we performing? KRI = is risk increasing? Both needed.
concepts.def: KPIs measure security program performance; KRIs measure risk levels for early warning.
concepts.ex: KPI: 98% patch compliance within SLA. KRI: 5 critical unpatched CVEs (risk rising).

concepts.tip: KPI = security scorecard. MTTD, MTTR, patch rate, vulnerability closure.
concepts.def: Quantifiable metrics measuring how effectively the security program is achieving its objectives.
concepts.ex: Mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to respond (MTTR), patch compliance rate.

concepts.def: KRIs are selected for their impact on the decisions of the senior leaders in the organization
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Key Performance and Risk Indicators
Technical report: methodology + findings + evidence + recommendations.
concepts.def: Documenting audit or assessment findings with methodology, evidence, risk ratings, and recommendations.
concepts.ex: Pen test report: executive summary, scope, methodology, findings by severity, remediation.

concepts.tip: Exec summary = business language. Risk, impact, and priorities. No jargon.
concepts.def: High-level non-technical summary of findings and risk for management and board audiences.
concepts.ex: One-page summary: 3 critical findings, estimated risk exposure, recommended priorities.

concepts.tip: Security personnel = the human layer of defense. Train and retain them.
concepts.def: Staff responsible for implementing, operating, and maintaining security controls and network infrastructure.
concepts.ex: CISO, security analysts, SOC operators, network engineers, and administrators.

concepts.tip: Facility access = badge + PIN + biometric. Mantrap for high security.
concepts.def: Systems controlling who can physically enter sensitive areas using badges, biometrics, and PINs.
concepts.ex: Badge readers at server room door; biometric scanner at data center entrance.

concepts.tip: Locks = first line of physical defense. Match strength to asset value.
concepts.def: Physical security devices preventing unauthorized access to facilities, hardware, or data.
concepts.ex: Key locks for offices; cipher locks for server rooms; padlocks for cabinets.

concepts.tip: Mechanical locks: pin tumbler (most secure), wafer (weak), disc detainer.
concepts.def: Traditional key-operated locks using pin tumbler, wafer tumbler, or disc detainer mechanisms.
concepts.ex: Pin tumbler (deadbolt), wafer (filing cabinet), disc detainer (bike lock).

concepts.tip: Wafer tumbler = simple, low security. Easily picked compared to pin tumbler.
concepts.def: Simpler mechanical lock using flat wafers instead of pins — lower security, common in cabinets and cars.
concepts.ex: Filing cabinet locks and older car door locks use wafer tumbler mechanism.

concepts.tip: Device locks = physically secure the hardware. Kensington = laptop standard.
concepts.def: Physical security for hardware including cable locks, port blockers, and chassis locks.
concepts.ex: Kensington cable lock securing laptop to desk; USB port blocker.

concepts.tip: Lock grade: Grade 1 = strongest. Match grade to asset sensitivity.
concepts.def: Lock security ratings from ANSI/BHMA or UL — Grade 1 (commercial high security) to Grade 3 (residential).
concepts.ex: Data center uses ANSI Grade 1 locks; office supply closet uses Grade 3.

concepts.tip: Personnel access: badge + PIN + escort policy for visitors.
concepts.def: Access cards, PINs, and biometrics controlling employee and visitor access to physical spaces.
concepts.ex: Employee badge opens lab door; visitor must be escorted by employee.

concepts.tip: External boundary: fence + bollards + lighting. CPTED principles.
concepts.def: Fences, bollards, lighting, walls, and natural barriers deterring unauthorized perimeter access.
concepts.ex: 6-foot fence with razor wire; bollards preventing vehicle ramming; motion lighting.

concepts.def: Fences six to seven feet high are considered too high to climb easily.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · External Boundary Protection Mechanisms
CCTV = deterrence + evidence. Placement matters — cover all entry points.
concepts.def: CCTV cameras providing surveillance coverage for deterrence and forensic evidence.
concepts.ex: IP cameras at entrance, server room, and parking lot with 90-day retention.

concepts.tip: Camera lenses: fixed (wide, cheap) vs. zoom (variable focal length).
concepts.def: Fixed-focal lenses (standard view, low cost) and zoom/varifocal lenses (adjustable field of view).
concepts.ex: Fixed lens for parking lot wide view; zoom lens to read license plates.

concepts.term: IDSs can be used to detect changes
concepts.tip: Physical IDS: motion + vibration + infrared sensors. Alerts on intrusion.
concepts.def: Physical intrusion detection systems using motion sensors, vibration detectors, and infrared to detect unauthorized entry.
concepts.ex: PIR motion sensor in server room triggers alarm if movement after hours.

concepts.tip: Asset inventory = know what you own. Can't protect what you can't see.
concepts.def: Comprehensive, up-to-date catalog of all hardware, software, data, and service assets.
concepts.ex: CMDB listing every server, VM, endpoint, and application with owner and location.

concepts.tip: Software tracking = license compliance + unauthorized app detection.
concepts.def: Tools monitoring software installations and licenses to ensure compliance and detect unauthorized software.
concepts.ex: ServiceNow ITAM tracks installed applications and license consumption.

concepts.tip: Asset mgmt = birth to death lifecycle. Track, protect, sanitize, dispose.
concepts.def: Lifecycle management of assets from procurement through deployment, maintenance, and disposal.
concepts.ex: New laptop provisioned per standard image; retired laptop degaussed and recycled.

concepts.tip: Config mgmt = maintain known-good baseline. Detect and fix drift.
concepts.def: Controlling and documenting the configuration of systems to maintain a known, secure state.
concepts.ex: CIS Benchmarks define secure baseline; Ansible enforces and audits drift.

concepts.tip: Change control: RFC → CAB → approve → test → deploy → review.
concepts.def: Formal procedure for requesting, reviewing, approving, testing, and implementing system changes.
concepts.ex: RFC submitted → CAB review → approval → test in staging → production deploy.

concepts.tip: Trusted recovery = fail safe. Security policy maintained through recovery.
concepts.def: System's ability to return to a secure, consistent state after a failure without violating security policy.
concepts.ex: System failure during transaction rolls back to last known-good checkpoint.

concepts.tip: After crash: validate integrity, review logs, restore from backup if needed.
concepts.def: Recovery procedures ensuring data integrity and security policy are maintained after unexpected failure.
concepts.ex: fsck validates filesystem; logs reviewed for evidence of corruption or attack.

concepts.tip: Recovery security = don't expose secrets while restoring. Dump files too.
concepts.def: Risk of exposing sensitive data, credentials, or configurations during system recovery processes.
concepts.ex: Memory dump during crash analysis may contain cleartext passwords in memory.

concepts.def: Locked-down systems are referred to as bastion hosts.
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Secure Resource Provisioning
MTBF = average time between failures. Higher = more reliable.
concepts.def: Average operating time between failures for a system or component — higher is better reliability.
concepts.ex: MTBF of 10,000 hours means server fails on average once every 417 days.

concepts.def: is a measure of how long we expect a piece of equipment to operate reliably
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Mean Time Between Failures

concepts.def: is the expected amount of time it will take to get a device fixed and back into production after its failure
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Network and Resource Availability
SPOF = one failure kills everything. Eliminate with redundancy.
concepts.def: Components whose failure causes complete system or service outage — must be eliminated or redundant.
concepts.ex: Single internet link, single power supply, single switch — all SPOFs.

concepts.tip: RAIT = RAID for tape. Multiple tapes = redundant backup storage.
concepts.def: RAIT — multiple tape drives used in parallel for backup redundancy, similar to RAID for disks.
concepts.ex: RAIT-1 mirrors data across two tape drives simultaneously.

concepts.tip: Backups: full (all), incremental (since last backup), differential (since full).
concepts.def: Copies of data made for recovery purposes — full, incremental, and differential backup strategies.
concepts.ex: Full backup Sunday; incremental Monday–Saturday; off-site tape rotation.

concepts.term: Summary of Technologies That Improve Resource Availability
concepts.tip: Availability tech: cluster + LB + RAID + UPS + geo-redundancy.
concepts.def: Clustering, load balancing, RAID, UPS, geographic redundancy, and failover systems.
concepts.ex: Active-passive cluster with load balancer and UPS ensures 99.99% uptime.

concepts.def: NIST Special Publication 800-137, “Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information Systems and Organizations,” defines information security continuous monitoring as “maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions.”
concepts.tip: Mind map CISSP · Preventing and Detecting
Vuln mgmt: scan → score → prioritize → remediate → verify.
concepts.def: Continuous program to identify, evaluate, prioritize, and remediate security weaknesses.
concepts.ex: Weekly Nessus scans → CVSS scoring → prioritize critical CVEs → patch within SLA.

concepts.tip: Software vulns: buffer overflow, SQLi, XSS, race condition. Patch and code review.
concepts.def: Security flaws in code including buffer overflows, SQL injection, race conditions, and logic errors.
concepts.ex: CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) = critical RCE in Log4j — patch immediately.

concepts.tip: Scanning = automated recon. Find what's open and what's vulnerable.
concepts.def: Automated discovery of network hosts, open ports, services, and known vulnerabilities.
concepts.ex: Nmap scans for open ports; Nessus identifies vulnerable service versions.

concepts.tip: Human vulns = people. Train, phish-test, and enforce least privilege.
concepts.def: Social engineering, insider threats, and phishing exploiting people as the weakest security link.
concepts.ex: Phishing email tricks employee into revealing VPN credentials.

concepts.tip: Unmanaged patching = chaos. Consistent gaps = consistent exposure.
concepts.def: Ad hoc patching approach leaving systems inconsistently patched and exposed to known vulnerabilities.
concepts.ex: No central tracking — some servers patched, others missed for months.

concepts.tip: Centralized patching = WSUS/SCCM. Consistent, tracked, reportable.
concepts.def: Enterprise tool (WSUS, SCCM, Jamf) deploying patches consistently and tracking compliance org-wide.
concepts.ex: SCCM deploys Windows patches to 5,000 endpoints within 72-hour SLA.

concepts.tip: Outsourced services = extend your risk. Vet vendors, audit contracts.
concepts.def: Third-party vendors providing IT or security services — require due diligence, contracts, and ongoing audits.
concepts.ex: Cloud provider SLA requires annual pen test; SOC 2 report reviewed annually.

concepts.tip: Reporting = document + escalate + notify. Timelines matter for compliance.
concepts.def: Documenting, escalating, and communicating security incidents to appropriate stakeholders and authorities.
concepts.ex: SOC analyst creates incident ticket; CISO notified; regulator notified within 72h.

concepts.term: Computer Forensics and Proper Collection of Evidence
concepts.tip: Forensics = image + hash + chain of custody. Don't touch original evidence.
concepts.def: Collecting digital evidence using forensically sound methods to maintain admissibility in legal proceedings.
concepts.ex: Create bit-for-bit disk image; verify with MD5/SHA hash before any analysis.

concepts.term: Scientific Working Group on Digital Evidence (SWGDE)
concepts.tip: SWGDE = sets the rules for how to handle digital evidence properly.
concepts.def: Organization developing standards and best practices for digital evidence collection and handling.
concepts.ex: SWGDE standards referenced by law enforcement for proper forensic procedures.

concepts.term: Different Types of Assessments an Investigator Can Perform
concepts.tip: Forensic assessments: network, media, software, hardware. Match to incident.
concepts.def: Network analysis, media analysis, software analysis, and hardware/embedded device analysis.
concepts.ex: Malware investigation: software analysis + network traffic capture + memory analysis.

concepts.tip: Network forensics = packet captures + flow logs. Catch attacker comms.
concepts.def: Capturing and analyzing network traffic logs and packets for forensic evidence of attacks.
concepts.ex: Wireshark PCAP shows C2 traffic; NetFlow logs show data exfiltration.

concepts.tip: Media analysis = dig into disks. Recover deleted files and artifacts.
concepts.def: Examining storage media (disks, USB, memory) for deleted files, artifacts, and digital evidence.
concepts.ex: FTK Imager recovers deleted files; Autopsy analyzes file system artifacts.

concepts.tip: Software analysis = reverse engineering. Static + dynamic analysis.
concepts.def: Reverse engineering malware and applications to understand behavior, capabilities, and attribution.
concepts.ex: IDA Pro disassembles ransomware binary to find C2 server address.

concepts.tip: Hardware forensics = firmware extraction + JTAG + chip-off analysis.
concepts.def: Examining firmware, embedded systems, and hardware for evidence or security vulnerabilities.
concepts.ex: JTAG debugging on IoT device to extract firmware and analyze security.

concepts.tip: Investigation types: admin, criminal, civil, regulatory. Different standards.
concepts.def: Administrative (policy), criminal (law enforcement), civil (litigation), and regulatory (compliance) investigations.
concepts.ex: Data breach: criminal (FBI) + regulatory (FTC) + civil (class action lawsuit).

concepts.tip: Field kit = portable forensics lab. Write blockers are essential.
concepts.def: Portable equipment for on-site evidence collection including write blockers, imaging drives, and documentation tools.
concepts.ex: Field kit: write blocker, portable forensic imager, evidence bags, chain of custody forms.

concepts.tip: Surveillance + search + seizure = legal evidence gathering. Warrants matter.
concepts.def: Legal procedures for gathering evidence — may require warrants; must follow proper chain of custody.
concepts.ex: Search warrant required before seizing corporate computers for criminal investigation.

concepts.tip: Surveillance = watch and record. Legal authorization needed in many contexts.
concepts.def: Systematic monitoring of individuals, systems, or networks for investigative or security purposes.
concepts.ex: Network surveillance captures attacker's lateral movement across systems.

concepts.tip: Business process recovery = functions first, then tech. Keep business running.
concepts.def: Restoring critical business functions and workflows after a disaster, not just IT systems.
concepts.ex: Recovery of order processing workflow even if using manual procedures initially.

concepts.tip: Recovery sites: hot (ready now), warm (hours), cold (days). Cost vs. speed.
concepts.def: Hot site (fully operational, immediate), warm site (hours to bring up), cold site (days to days).
concepts.ex: Financial firm uses hot site for zero downtime; retailer uses warm site.

concepts.tip: Supply recovery = vendor SLAs + spare parts + software license portability.
concepts.def: Ensuring hardware, software licenses, and vendor supply chains can be restored after a disaster.
concepts.ex: Vendor agreements guarantee replacement hardware within 4 hours of disaster declaration.

concepts.tip: Backup strategy: 3-2-1 rule. Three copies, two media, one off-site.
concepts.def: On-site (fast recovery) plus off-site (disaster protection) — follow 3-2-1 backup rule.
concepts.ex: 3 copies, 2 media types, 1 off-site — tape vault 50 miles from data center.

concepts.tip: Online backup = continuous replication. Near-zero RPO. Expensive.
concepts.def: Continuous real-time data replication to remote storage achieving near-zero RPO.
concepts.ex: Continuous Data Protection (CDP) replicates every write to cloud storage.

concepts.tip: Electronic backup = disk-based. Faster than tape. Deduplication helps.
concepts.def: Disk-based backup systems replacing tape with faster backup and restore capabilities.
concepts.ex: Veeam backup to disk; deduplicated storage appliance with cloud tier.

concepts.tip: Electronic vaulting = digital off-site backup. Automate tape-to-cloud.
concepts.def: Automated batch transfer of backup data to a remote secure facility over network.
concepts.ex: Nightly backup files transmitted electronically to off-site vault — no tape transport.

concepts.tip: End-user recovery = get employees working again. Desktops, apps, data.
concepts.def: Restoring user workstations, applications, and data access for employees to resume work after disaster.
concepts.ex: Golden image deployment restores 500 laptops from DR image in 2 hours.

concepts.tip: Liability = legal accountability. Due care = reasonable standard.
concepts.def: Legal responsibility for harm caused by negligence, breach of duty of care, or failure to act reasonably.
concepts.ex: Company liable for breach if court finds security was below reasonable standard.

concepts.tip: Liability scenarios: breach → lawsuit + regulatory fine + reputational damage.
concepts.def: Data breach, privacy violation, third-party compromise, and negligent security leading to legal action.
concepts.ex: Hospital breached — patients sue for negligence; regulators fine for HIPAA violation.

concepts.tip: Contracts = define who is responsible. SLA, NDA, MOU, BAA.
concepts.def: SLAs, NDAs, MOUs, and BAs defining security responsibilities, obligations, and liability between parties.
concepts.ex: Business Associate Agreement (BAA) required with HIPAA-covered entities.

concepts.tip: Vendor procurement = security questionnaire + SOC 2 + right to audit.
concepts.def: Due diligence on third-party security posture before engagement — questionnaires, certifications, audits.
concepts.ex: Vendor must provide SOC 2 Type II report and complete security questionnaire.

concepts.tip: DR personnel = assign roles before disaster. Train everyone, not just IT.
concepts.def: Assigning DR roles and responsibilities and training staff so recovery can proceed without key individuals.
concepts.ex: DR team: recovery coordinator, IT lead, communications lead, business unit leads.

concepts.tip: DR assessment = triage after disaster. What's lost? What's next?
concepts.def: Evaluating the extent of damage after a disaster to determine priorities and recovery sequence.
concepts.ex: Post-disaster assessment: data center flooded — 80% hardware loss, invoke hot site.

concepts.tip: Restoration = rebuild from backups and images. Test restores beforehand!
concepts.def: Rebuilding systems and services from backups and recovery procedures to restore normal operations.
concepts.ex: Restore databases from last-known-good backup; rebuild servers from golden images.

concepts.tip: DR communications = who to call, when, and with what message.
concepts.def: Maintaining contact with staff, customers, regulators, and partners during and after a disaster.
concepts.ex: Crisis communication plan: phone tree, backup email domain, public status page.

concepts.tip: Emergency mgmt = life-safety first. Evacuation plans and wardens.
concepts.def: Coordinating organizational response to life-safety emergencies protecting employees and visitors.
concepts.ex: Fire marshal directs evacuation; emergency coordinator calls first responders.

concepts.tip: OEP = the building evacuation and shelter-in-place plan.
concepts.def: Occupant Emergency Plan — procedures for safely evacuating or sheltering building occupants during emergencies.
concepts.ex: OEP covers fire evacuation, bomb threat shelter-in-place, and medical emergencies.

concepts.tip: Travel security = threat brief + loaner device + VPN + encrypted comms.
concepts.def: Security measures and guidelines for employees traveling to high-risk areas.
concepts.ex: Pre-trip briefing on local threats; use loaner laptops; avoid public Wi-Fi.
